blk_part_01_part_1_why_a_small_table_mak.text: Because the game is so fast, many players think carefully about their racket. A racket has two main parts. The blade is the wooden part with the handle. The rubbers are the sheets on each side of the blade. Every player chooses a different mix, and you are the expert on your own racket. When you talk about it, you can explain what your blade is like and why you chose it. You can also compare the rubber on your forehand side with the rubber on your backhand side. Then you can say what you want your racket to help you with, such as spin, speed or control.

blk_part_02_part_2_training_the_legs_and.text: So serious training also builds the body. Exercises like squats and hinges build general strength. A hinge is a movement where you bend forward from the hips. Unilateral exercises, such as split squats, train one leg at a time. This matters because players often push off from one leg to move sideways. Plyometric exercises are quick, jumping movements. Pogo hops and lateral bounds, which are jumps to the side, improve quick footwork. They also help the split-step, the small hop that gets a player ready to move in any direction.

blk_part_04_part_4_a_sport_built_on_scho.text: Adult club life is a different story, and every club is different. Some people continue after school. Others stop for years and then come back. Your own experience is the best guide here. When you describe your adult club, you can talk about where and when you play, and who you play with. You can also explain what a normal practice includes. Then you can compare matches in your school club with matches in your adult club, and say how the friendships feel different.
